nerklärung_Bezug_Russland-0422 Entsprechend der Verordnung (EU) 2022/576 dürfen öffentlichen Aufträge und Konzessionen nach dem 9. April 2022 nicht an Personen oder Unternehmen vergeben werden, die einen Bezug zu Russland im Sinne der Vorschrift aufweisen. Dies umfasst sowohl unmittelbar als Bewerber, Bieter oder Auftragnehmer auftretende Personen oder Unternehmen als auch mittelbar, mit mehr als zehn Prozent, gemessen am Auftragswert, beteiligte Unterauftragnehmer, Lieferanten oder Eignungsverleiher. Ein Bezug zu Russland im Sinne der Vorschrift besteht a) durch die russische Staatsangehörigkeit des Bewerbers/Bieters oder die Niederlassung des Bewerbers/Bieters in Russland, b) durch die Beteiligung einer natürlichen Person oder eines Unternehmens, auf die eines der Kriterien nach Buchstabe a zutrifft, am Bewerber/Bieter über das Halten von Anteilen im Umfang von mehr als 50 Prozent, c) durch das Handeln der Bewerber /Bieter im Namen oder auf Anweisung von Personen oder Unternehmen, auf die die Kriterien der Buchstaben a und/oder b zutreffen. Bereits vor dem 9. April 2022 geschlossene Verträge mit solchen Personen oder Unternehmen mit Bezug zu Russland dürfen nur bis zum 10. Oktober 2022 fortgeführt werden. Käsikirjadega saab tutvuda Google Drive kaustast Täpsem ajakava lepitakse eduka pakkujaga ühe kuu jooksul alates lepingu sõlmimisest. Pakkuja ja tellija lepivad kokku kooskõlastusringide tähtaegadest, vastutajatest ja kontaktisikutest. Ajakava koostamisel lähtutakse alljärgnevatest punktidest 5.3-5.11. Pakkuja töö hõlmab vähemalt järgmisi kooskõlastatud tööetappe: käsikirjade terviklik ülevaatus ja toimetamisvajaduse kaardistamine; ühe kooliastme klasside terminoloogia, struktuuri ja vormistuslahenduste ühtlustamine; kujunduskontseptsiooni ja näidiskülgede koostamine ning kooskõlastamine tellija ja autoritega; illustratsioonide, fotode, ikoonide ja muude visuaalsete elementide loomine või hankimine; esmane küljendus; katsetamise ja retsenseerimise tagasiside alusel muudatuste tegemine; lõplik keeleline ja tehniline korrektuur; trükifailide ettevalmistamine ja tellijapoolne kinnitamine enne trükki. Osades 1–3 kirjeldatud lõplike materjalide trükkimise eel viiakse läbi õppekomplektide katsetamine, milleks on vaja ette valmistada ja trükkida katsetuseksemplarid ja saata need katsetajatele. Introduction The Administrative Office of the United States Courts (AO) is seeking contractor services for the printing and mailing of the following Internal Revenue Service (IRS) information returns: • W-2, Wage and Tax Statement • 1099-R, Distributions from Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit-Sharing Plans, IRAs, Insurance Contracts, etc. • 1099-INT, Interest Income • 1099-MISC, Miscellaneous Income • 1099-NEC Nonemployee Compensation The printing and mailing support service will allow the Federal Judiciary to accomplish the requirement on the annual IRS tax reporting obligations. This contract will be for printing and mailing services ONLY and DOES NOT include the contractor providing any other tax-related services. The AO will provide ready-to-print and mail Portable Document File (PDF) data files to the contractor with all W-2 and 1099 boxes prepopulated with the appropriate tax information along with appropriate instructions of each tax form. The contractor shall provide the judiciary with electronic copies of all W-2s and 1099s printed and mailed to the recipients. The contractor must have the capability to securely receive and store electronic files from the AO using AO approved encryption methods such as Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) for files in-transit and hard disk encryption for files at-rest. The contractor shall make available their secure file system for remote AO security testing and inspection by the AO DCIO Information Assurance Branch immediately after award, and prior to any work performed under this contract. In the event the contractor’s system is deemed incapable of performance, and the contractor is unable to fully comply with the requirements to securely receive and store electronic files from the AO, the results shall be relayed to the AO Department of Administrative Services (DAS) Acquisition Management Office (AMO) for potential contract action, to include immediate termination. The contractor will print the information returns as instructed by the Judiciary. The printed information return, if any, will be bi- folded/tri-folded with the name and address from the information return facing up. The contractor shall use a mailing label or panel with the recipient’s name and address as stated on the form, accompanied by a USPS barcode. The contractor shall adjust the recipient’s address to a more accurate address in accordance with the USPS database to enhance delivery assurance. The information return envelope will have the words “IMPORTANT TAX DOCUMENT ENCLOSED” clearly showing on the front of the envelope. The address for each recipient and the AO’s return mailing address must be fully visible if a suitable double window envelope is not used. Each envelope is to be completely sealed if placed into an envelope. Each sealed envelope is to be stamped using the AO's USPS bulk mailing stamp; for government certificate/permit mailing by pre- printed permit and penalty certificate on the envelopes. The contractor may use pressure seal paper if the document mailed to the recipient complies with IRS tax form requirements. The contractor will batch the sealed and stamped envelopes and deliver them to a USPS facility to be mailed. There shall be no loss of control over the stuffed envelopes at any time. The batch must remain under exclusive control of the contractor until it is received by the USPS. The contractor may use machine control marks (2D Barcodes) to enhance quality assurance. The contractor shall obtain properly completed and signed Postal Service Form(s) 3606, Certificate of Bulk Mailing – International, and 3606-D, Certificate of Bulk Mailing – Domestic, as proof of delivery to USPS. LE: files/Attach_1_-_Blood_Transfusion_Services_SOW.pdf ===== Statement of Work For Transfusion Services 20 October 2026 I. Background: The 88th Medical Group Transfusion Services requires blood components and references lab transfusion testing services. The supplier shall provide blood products and reference blood transfusion services (testing) to support the blood supply in case of emergency situations and inpatient and outpatient care at the WPAFB Medical Center when requested for a period of 5 years at the prices in the approved price list. II. Minimum Technical Requirements: The supplier shall provide blood products and reference transfusion testing that are time dependent with immediate response and expedience to treat critical patients. The supplier must operate 24/7 as the 88th Medical Group (MDG) is a 24/7 operation; this service must be available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including holidays and weekends. The supplier shall provide rapid shipment of blood products when the 88 MDG Transfusion Services in-house inventory is in need to support critical patients. The one-hour turnaround time for testing is a mission-critical requirement. The blood supplier shall deliver routine blood products ordered on a STAT basis within one (1) hour of the blood sup

eipt of an emergent request for blood products. The required completion point is delivery to the Transfusion Services department. The supplier must fulfill our request with the ordered product with appropriate compatible blood type, applicable testing, and requested quantities. Any unforeseen delays are understandable; however, the ultimate goal is for the delivering agency to aim for the <1 hour delivery time. An appropriate transmittal list is required with each delivery. If emergent requests are unable to be consistently met, it could mean critical failure for our hospital's life-saving capabilities. The supplier shall have 24/7 reference laboratory testing capabilities for patients anticipating transfusions or medical treatment. The supplier must be licensed by the Food & Drug Administration (FDA) and follow American Association of Blood Bank (AABB) standards. The supplier must notify the 88th MDG Transfusion Services of all unexpected/abnormal tests from blood products supplied by them. The supplier shall provide look-back notifications to the 88th MDG as required by 21 CFR 610.48 (b)(3): (a) within three (3) calendar days if blood collected from a donor who tested negative at the time of donation but tests reactive for evidence of HIV or HCV infection on a later do
